inspection.evidenceScope: PARTIAL: Public doctor catalog unavailable or invalid. Generated cases are based on documented routes and acceptance criteria only. Unavailable live endpoints are NOT verified. No authenticated workflows were crawled.

cases.title: Successful registration with valid unique details
cases.preconditions: Visitor is on the registration page and provides unique user details.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/register with valid name, unique email, valid mobile number, and valid password.
Check the response status code and body.
cases.testData: Name: John Doe, Email: john.doe.unique@example.com, Mobile: +15552345678, Password: SecurePassword123
cases.expectedResult: Account is successfully created and a valid JWT token is returned in the response.

cases.title: Registration rejection due to missing required fields
cases.preconditions: Visitor attempts to register without filling out all mandatory fields.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/register omitting the email field.
Inspect the HTTP response status and error message.
cases.testData: Name: John Doe, Email: , Mobile: +15552345678, Password: SecurePassword123
cases.expectedResult: Request is rejected with a 400 bad request status and an indication that missing fields are required.

cases.title: Registration rejection due to short password
cases.preconditions: Visitor attempts to register using a password that does not meet minimum length criteria.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/register with a password shorter than the required minimum length.
Inspect the HTTP response status and error message.
cases.testData: Name: John Doe, Email: john.short@example.com, Mobile: +15552345678, Password: 123
cases.expectedResult: Request is rejected with a 400 bad request status indicating the password is too short.

cases.title: Boundary test for password length at minimum threshold
cases.preconditions: Visitor attempts to register using a password exactly at the boundary length.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/register with a password matching the exact minimum allowed length.
Verify if the account creation succeeds.
cases.testData: Name: Jane Doe, Email: jane.boundary@example.com, Mobile: +15558765432, Password: Pass1
cases.expectedResult: Account is successfully created if the length meets the minimum policy, or rejected appropriately if it falls under.

proposedCaseReviews.originalTitle: Successful registration with valid unique details
proposedCaseReviews.issue: Original positive case has +1 international phone format, while backend requires a 10-digit Indian phone starting 6–9. API JSON field is phone, not mobile.

proposedEdits.testData: Request JSON: {"name":"John Doe","email":"john.doe.unique@example.com","phone":"9876543210","password":"SecurePassword123"}. Use unique synthetic email and isolated test database.
steps: Prepare synthetic patient details with unique email and valid-format 10-digit Indian phone number.
POST JSON to /api/v1/auth/register using name, email, phone and password.
Assert HTTP 201; response success=true, token nonempty and user email matches.
Verify an account exists in the isolated database and that the password is not exposed in the response.
proposedEdits.expectedResult: HTTP 201; success=true; nonempty JWT token; created user details returned, without password.

proposedCaseReviews.proposedReviewerNote: This positive case targets valid registration but would fail with its original +1 phone data; corrected the field to phone and used a valid-format 10-digit Indian number so the success assertion is meaningful.

proposedCaseReviews.originalTitle: Registration rejection due to missing required fields
proposedCaseReviews.issue: Omitted email is appropriate, but the original +1 phone creates an additional invalid input, so a 400 does not isolate the missing-email validation.

proposedEdits.testData: Request JSON: {"name":"John Doe","phone":"9876543210","password":"SecurePassword123"}. Do not include the email property.
steps: Prepare otherwise valid synthetic data but omit the email property completely.
POST JSON to /api/v1/auth/register.
Assert HTTP 400 and response message says name, email, password and phone are required.
Check that the isolated database contains no newly registered account.
proposedEdits.expectedResult: HTTP 400; success=false; missing-required-fields validation message; no account created.

proposedCaseReviews.proposedReviewerNote: AI-002 covers missing required email but includes invalid phone data. I would change the phone to a valid value and omit email entirely so the failed registration tests the intended validation rule.

proposedCaseReviews.originalTitle: Registration rejection due to short password
proposedCaseReviews.issue: Original short password is below minimum but has no precise 7-character boundary and an additional invalid phone; improving one invalid input at a time makes it reliable.

steps: Prepare otherwise valid synthetic registration fields with a seven-character password.
POST JSON to /api/v1/auth/register.
Assert HTTP 400 and a message stating password must be at least 8 characters.
Verify no patient account is created in the isolated database.
proposedEdits.expectedResult: HTTP 400; success=false; password minimum-length error; no account created.

proposedCaseReviews.proposedReviewerNote: This is an important negative case, but the extra invalid mobile value could confuse the result. I would use an otherwise valid registration and a seven-character password to check the minimum-length boundary.

proposedCaseReviews.originalTitle: Boundary test for password length at minimum threshold
proposedCaseReviews.issue: The original sample password Pass1 contains five characters, not exactly eight; phone is invalid and expected result is conditional instead of specific.

steps: Prepare valid unique synthetic registration data with the password Pass1234 (eight characters).
POST JSON to /api/v1/auth/register.
Assert HTTP 201; response success=true and a JWT token is returned.
Verify account was created in an isolated database.
proposedEdits.expectedResult: HTTP 201; account created and JWT token returned, because an exactly eight-character password meets the minimum-length policy.

proposedCaseReviews.proposedReviewerNote: The original test claims to cover the eight-character minimum but supplies only five characters. I would correct the password to exactly eight, use a valid phone field and expect successful account creation.

proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.criterion: Valid unique details create account and JWT
proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.manualAssessment: requires human verification of TP-001 expected result
proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.suggestedEvidence: AI-001 and AI-004 are intended positive cases, but both original test data are invalid; AI-004 also misstates password boundary. TP-001 specifies valid registration, but independently check its full expected result for JWT verification.

proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.criterion: Missing fields or short password are rejected.
proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.manualAssessment: covered at scenario-design level by TP-002 and TP-003
proposedAcceptanceCriteriaNotes.suggestedEvidence: AI-002 and AI-003 target required-field and weak-password rejection, but each original case includes an invalid US-format phone that confounds validation. TP-002 covers missing required registration data and TP-003 covers seven-character password rejection.
